verdicts.decision_note: The client defines DCDC1 as the 3.3V, 2A primary system rail and identifies its concrete downstream loads.
The source discusses an untested LED voltage specification and does not establish that DCDC1 powers the LEDs.
The source concerns GPIO control of the separate 5V boost rail and does not modify DCDC1 regulation or its existing load state.
The acceptance concerns replacing INA219 with INA3221 for rail-current monitoring, which belongs to REQ_POWER_RAIL_CURRENT_MONITORING rather than DCDC1 regulation.
The client explicitly configures DCDC1 for 3.4V through I2C to preserve the 3.3V system rail after the Schottky drop; no prior key becomes stale.
The client explicitly moves the SK6812 LEDs onto the 3.3V rail, adding them as a concrete DCDC1-served load.
The tentative integrated-board proposal does not specify DCDC1 loads or preserve a Schottky-ORing compensation requirement, so the proposed updates exceed the source.
First concrete production failure: two of three boards showed an unstable L3 voltage instead of the required 3.3V.
First concrete post-failure verification of the startup path: all three integrated samples produced approximately 3.3V and ran the ESP32.
Distinct post-startup failure: USB-powered flash and WiFi load transients collapsed DCDC1 below 2.5V, and one output stage later degraded and failed.
